Legionella Control Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Sections reordered for readability; no requirement changed.*

Responsibility

The Facilities Lead maintains the legionella risk assessment and monitoring log for every site.

Water temperature monitoring

Hot water outlets are checked monthly to confirm they reach 50°C within one minute at the tap. Cold water outlets are checked to confirm they remain below 20°C.

Flushing of little-used outlets

Any outlet unused for more than a week is flushed for at least 2 minutes to prevent stagnation.

Control programme

The responsible person maintains a written scheme covering hot and cold-water temperatures, sentinel outlets, little-used outlets, shower-head cleaning and the response to an out-of-range result. Maintenance staff record each check against the asset and outlet identifier so a missed check can be distinguished from a compliant reading. A room closure, plumbing alteration or prolonged vacancy triggers a fresh assessment before the outlet returns to use.

Out-of-range response

A temperature or hygiene result outside the written scheme is reported to the registered manager and facilities lead on the same working day. The outlet is isolated where continued use could expose a resident or staff member, remedial flushing or engineering work is commissioned, and reopening requires a documented satisfactory recheck. A suspected case of legionellosis is escalated immediately through infection-control and public-health routes rather than managed as routine maintenance.

Assurance and records

The registered manager reviews the log monthly for missed checks and repeated marginal readings. The facilities lead reviews contractor reports, corrective actions and trend data quarterly. Risk assessments, schematics, monitoring records, laboratory results and remedial-work evidence are retained together so an auditor can reconstruct the control history for each water system.

Medication Fridge Breakdown Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 April 2025. Escalation changed to also require a call to the supplying pharmacy, not only the on-call manager.*

If the fridge fails

Keep the affected fridge closed, do not move stock on assumption, and call both the on-call manager and the supplying pharmacy (a new requirement — the previous version only required the on-call manager) for advice on whether the stock remains usable; see Immediate containment below for the full response, including when a validated alternative storage location may be used.

Immediate containment

When the medicines-fridge temperature is outside range or the unit fails, staff keep the door closed, note the current and available minimum/maximum readings, label the unit not for use and inform the responsible nurse or manager. Stock is not moved into a domestic refrigerator or discarded on assumption. A validated alternative refrigerator or insulated container is prepared where authorised.

Clinical and pharmacy advice

Staff list every affected medicine, batch where available, storage requirement and estimated exposure time and obtain product-specific pharmacy or manufacturer advice. The decision to use, quarantine or replace each item is recorded. Time-critical doses are escalated so an alternative supply or clinically appropriate plan can be arranged without bypassing prescribing controls.

Recovery and assurance

The failed unit is inspected and must demonstrate a stable compliant temperature before return to service. Quarantined stock remains segregated until a documented decision is made. Temperature records, exposure assessment, advice, stock disposition, engineer report and any omitted-dose or incident record are retained together, and repeated failures trigger equipment replacement review.

*Supersedes the version effective 1 April 2025. Escalation changed to also require a call to the supplying pharmacy, not only the on-call manager.*

If the fridge fails

Keep the affected fridge closed, do not move stock on assumption, and call both the on-call manager and the supplying pharmacy (a new requirement — the previous version only required the on-call manager) for advice on whether the stock remains usable; see Immediate containment below for the full response, including when a validated alternative storage location may be used.

When the medicines-fridge temperature is outside range or the unit fails, staff keep the door closed, note the current and available minimum/maximum readings, label the unit not for use and inform the responsible nurse or manager. Staff list every affected medicine, batch where available, storage requirement and estimated exposure time and obtain product-specific pharmacy or manufacturer advice. The failed unit is inspected and must demonstrate a stable compliant temperature before return to service. Quarantined stock remains segregated until a documented decision is made. Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a resident's clothing and site linen is laundered at Alderbridge Care Group. It
applies to every site's laundry operation.

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately from site linen, clearly labelled, and washed at a
temperature appropriate to the fabric, while soiled linen follows a specific infection-control hot-wash
standard.

Definitions

**Resident's own clothing** clothing belonging to and worn by an individual resident, laundered separately
and returned to them. **Site linen** bedding, towels and similar items not tied to a specific resident.
**Soiled linen** linen contaminated with a bodily fluid, requiring the infection-control hot-wash standard.

Roles and responsibilities

**Laundry staff** launder a resident's clothing separately, labelled, and follow the correct wash
temperature for the item type. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled linen correctly for separate handling.
**The registered manager** ensures the laundry operation meets this procedure's standard.

1. Label every resident's clothing clearly on admission, and again promptly if a label is lost or becomes
illegible.

2. Launder a resident's own clothing separately from another resident's items and from site linen, at a
temperature appropriate to the fabric.

3. Wash soiled linen at 60 degrees Celsius, following the infection-control hot-wash standard, handled
separately from the point of collection.

4. Return laundered clothing to the correct resident promptly, checking labelling at the point of return.

5. Report a persistent labelling or mix-up issue to the registered manager for investigation.
